_meta.description: Gold standard for L1 Centhini extraction pilot: the studied-species subset from Nafayu et al. 2025, Table 1.
_meta.compiled_by: Claude (read from PDF Table 1) — hand-curated reference, verify against source before publication

provenance.citation: Nafayu Y.H.D., Kintoko K., Pratama A.N.W., Josafat A., Raharjo A.M., Triatmoko B., Nawiyanto N., Wangchuk P., Keller P.A., Nugraha A.S. (2025). Bioprospecting medicinal plants of Centhini: Javanese ancient manuscript. Ethnobotany Research and Applications, 31: 1-42.
provenance.source_text_they_used: Kamajaya (1985) Latin transliteration of the COMPLETE 12-volume Serat Centhini (suluk tambangraras), Yayasan Centhini, Yogyakarta. 3500 pages.

caveats: This file holds the 32 species that Nafayu reports as having modern pharmacological study (their Table 1 + discussion). The full 82-species inventory is NOT cleanly text-extractable: ~50 species appear only inside figures (Fig 5 X-axis, Fig 7 Sankey) as images, not machine-readable text.
Abstract says 'twelve diseases'; Table 1 footnote lists ELEVEN use categories (no 12th). Internal inconsistency in the source paper — not resolved here.
Use categories follow Staub et al. classification, NOT our disease_ontology.json categories. Cross-mapping is future work.

Latin names are as printed by Nafayu; authorities stripped here. Some differ from our KG canonical names (e.g. Nigella sativa vs our 'Nigella sativum'; Curcuma longa vs 'Curcuma domestica'). Reconcile before any recall computation.
